newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil cargoes stable after Russians trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil cargoes stable after Russians trade.

text.p: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil cargoes were stable on Thursday as dealers eyed continued avails of Russian straight-run material which faced healthy demand, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $120 fob ARA and sellers were later heard at the same level.
A Russian M-100, with low water and sailing on the Lami, was heard sold to a trader at around $119 cif NWE.
Other M-100 cargoes, with higher water levels, were expected to fetch prices a couple of dollars below that.
On Tuesday an ARA refiner bought an E-4 cargo from a trader. The cargo, loading on the Blue Star between November 3 and 5, was sold at $3.50 above the three means of publilshed quotes.
Utility players said they were receiving offers of Russian and non-Russian material at around $118 cif NWE.

Low sulphur markets were heard subdued following a deal on Tuesday in which a large Italian utility bought a very prompt 25,000-tonne cargo from a trader at a price that was half fixed at $130 cif Italy, and half calculated on a floating basis. -- Nicholas Shaxson, London newsroom +44 171 542 8167
